messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated cross-region routing churn detected between us-east, us-west, and eu (smart-routing policy 'auto-fallback-v2'). 5xx increase + healthcheck flaps. Pager triggered. https://monitoring.redwood.internal/alerts/CR-1923456789 :rotating_light:
anna (oncall): saw it. investigating now. beginning triage.
raj (sre): joining. can you post the highest-error logs? are we seeing model variant mismatches too?
maya (runtime): initial reports show probes toggling health state between regions every ~20s. routing engine flips traffic -> causes cascade.
sam (product): customer-impact? any visible API errors for hosted users?
lucy (cs): a couple of paying customers flagged increased latency and occasional 502s, reported via support@ — I have the list, forwarding to oncall.
anna (oncall): thanks @lucy. collecting traces. can we pin traffic to a single region as a temporary mitigation?
raj (sre): yes. recommend pinning affected routes to us-east (primary) for 10m while we stabilize.
maya (runtime): agree. but watch capacity - us-east burst might saturate. will throttle new sessions if needed.
deploy-bot: Scheduled action: route-controller.pin-route --route "api/v1/generate" --region us-east --duration 10m --by incident-bot
anna (oncall): executing now.
anna (oncall): DONE: routing pinned to us-east for /generate. Observability: request rate shifted, error count dropping slightly.
raj (sre): logs show healthcheck endpoint returning 503 intermittently from eu nodes. Stack traces point to KV cache overflow during probe window.
maya (runtime): that matches a recent change: canary config for health-check timeout was reduced to 2s in auto-fallback-v2 policy. Should be 5s.
sam (product): wait, that change was from pre-release yesterday, meant for limited canary but looks like it propagated.
anna (oncall): who pushed the policy change? audit?
maya (runtime): `git rev-parse` of routing-policy repo shows commit a1b2c3 by maya, merged via CI at 1923456700. The merge job should have been gated but a tag mis-match allowed global rollout.
raj (sre): OK root cause: aggressive health-check timeout caused transient probe failures -> routing controller considered nodes unhealthy -> traffic flipped -> cross-region rebalancing caused backend pressure -> more probe timeouts -> loop.
lucy (cs): customers noticing latency spikes and occasional 502s for ~17 minutes. I opened support tickets and prioritised two enterprise customers.
anna (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) keep pin in place, 2) revert policy timeout to 5s in routing config, 3) increase health debounce to 3 probes, 4) roll small canary to 5% after verifying.
raj (sre): I'll handle step 2 and 3. Maya can validate runtime behavior.
maya (runtime): applying config revert now.
maya (runtime): CLI: ``routing-ctl apply --policy auto-fallback-v2 --set health_timeout=5s --set health_debounce=3``
maya (runtime): patch applied. pushing to control plane.
anna (oncall): monitoring: health flaps decreasing, routing controller showing fewer failover events.
raj (sre): also increasing probe backoff: ``kubectl -n routing patch configmap fallback-config -p '{"data":{"probe_backoff":"4s"}}'``
raj (sre): applied. beginning cool-down window before unpinning.
lucy (cs): telling customers: "We've applied a configuration rollback to stabilize routing and are monitoring. We'll provide timeline and postmortem."
sam (product): good. we should include apology and credit for incident priority. Also list mitigations.
anna (oncall): estimate impact window: 00:16 - 00:40 UTC (24 min). I got traces showing spike start at 1923456789 and stabilization at 1923456970.
raj (sre): confirm: backend cpu on eu nodes spiked during the flip. KV cache thrashing observed. I'll add autoscale headroom guard for eu while we validate.
maya (runtime): temporary autoscale: ``infra-ctl autoscale set --region eu --min-instances 4``
maya (runtime): autoscale set.
deploy-bot: Action recorded: autoscale set for eu min=4 by maya at 1923456915.
anna (oncall): alerting: we still have a couple of legacy routes using older policy. scanning for matches.
raj (sre): also adding an emergency runbook step: if routing loop recurs, set `policy.disable_auto_fallback=true` to stop policy-driven flips while we TTR.
anna (oncall): good idea. I'll add that to incident notes.
lucy (cs): CS update posted to affected customers. Some asked for ETA for postmortem. I'll coordinate with product.
sam (product): planning postmortem. assign owners: maya -> runtime root cause and test gaps; raj -> mitigations and SLO review; anna -> timeline and customer impact; lucy -> customer comms.
anna (oncall): unpin traffic? what's the safe condition?
raj (sre): wait for 15m of stable probe pass, error rate < 10% of baseline and no repeat of flip events.
maya (runtime): we hit 15m stable at 1923457055. metrics show error rate back to baseline.
anna (oncall): unpinning /generate now.
anna (oncall): DONE: route unpinned. routing controller resuming normal balancing.
raj (sre): watching for second-order effects. no new spikes in last 5m.
lucy (cs): customers acknowledged, some relieved. closing support P1s.
sam (product): next steps: CI gate fix to prevent canary config from global rollout, add simulation test for healthcheck timeout drift, and update routing runbooks.
maya (runtime): I'll open PRs for gating + add unit test for policy propagation.
raj (sre): I'll add a monitoring rule: if region health toggles >3 times in 10m, suppress auto-fallback and page SRE.
anna (oncall): thanks team. I will mark incident resolved after doc + handoff. Incident created CR-1923456789.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: CR-1923456789 - Multi-region healthcheck flap; root cause: aggressive health-check timeout in auto-fallback-v2 policy + canary gating bug. Duration: 00:00:16 to 00:24:??. Postmortem owner: sam (product). :white_check_mark:
